image_prompt.text: Large floating masses and crystalline shards scattered through the clash space, letting a retreating fighter break combat lock
Narrow spans and rift mouths that funnel fighters together into predictable flashpoints
Terrain and structures welded so strikes crater them and ultimate attacks can level whole mountains
The Time Nest — a colossal hyper-structure hanging in the void, composed to be framed from every approach
High-fidelity set pieces — holographic galaxies, volumetric nebulae, ray-traced energy — isolated into clusters so they can be streamed in within visual range rather than rendered everywhere at once
Jagged purple and black Dimensional Rifts standing as physical portal markers, each opening onto a separate reality
Planet surfaces reached through the rifts: glowing alien jungles, shattered crystalline wastelands, oceans of liquid plasma

layout_placement.text: Rift markers paired to separate galaxy maps, sited at the edges of the hub

notes: The buildable ask is a galaxy, not an arena. Action owns the shape and its shapes are all bounded clash spaces, so the combat modules are expressed and the universe around them is not.

Scale: the prompt demands an unbounded procedurally generated universe and instructs that boundaries not be rendered. No band can hold that and one framed image cannot either. The decomposed alternative is the Time Nest hub as one map plus per-planet maps behind the rifts, which is why P4 is on the route.
The stated count of portals — 990,100 quadrillion alternate realities — cannot be carried anywhere; teleporter-link has no cardinality.
Engine-level demands (Unreal cinematic tier, ray tracing, 8K, PBR, non-Roblox aesthetics, custom high-poly avatars) are outside what a layout can honour and are recorded as constraints only.
choke-bottleneck comes from the preset and fights the prompt: funnels do not funnel anyone when every player has unrestricted 360-degree flight.

open_questions.ask: A single image cannot frame an infinite galaxy — should we build the Time Nest hub first, or one planet surface, and add the rest as separate maps?
What ends a session — is this an endless open universe, or are there objectives on each planet?

theme: Ultra-realistic cosmic sci-fi — physically based metals, ray-traced energy, deliberately not Roblox-styled

coverage_missing.ask: Which single location should we build first — the hub, or one planet?
Is there any objective, or is it free-roam combat?
Do the rifts lead to separate maps, or to zones of one map?
Is the combat player versus player, versus AI, or both?

answers.ask: A single image cannot frame an infinite galaxy — should we build the Time Nest hub first, or one planet surface, and add the rest as separate maps?
answers.answer: Build the Time Nest hub first as the central cosmic structure, with portals leading to separate planet maps as the initial representation of the wider Xenoverse.

answers.ask: What ends a session — is this an endless open universe, or are there objectives on each planet?
answers.answer: This is an endless open universe; the prompt does not call for planet objectives or a session-ending condition.
